assembly.title: Assembly
assembly.description: The assembly key of idtrack's organism table.

releases.title: Releases
releases.description: The releases at which the graph holds data of it.

serves.title: Serves
serves.description: The releases it serves (is the assembly whose annotation counts).

external_databases.title: External Databases
external_databases.description: The external databases of the graph on it.

synonym_databases.title: Synonym Databases
synonym_databases.description: Those of `external_databases` that record synonyms (read under the database's name: `from_database` covers them).

AssemblyDescription.title: AssemblyDescription
AssemblyDescription.description: One genome assembly of a loaded graph.

from_release.title: From Release
from_release.description: The release the identifiers are read at; `null`: inferred.

to_release.title: To Release
to_release.description: The target release; `null`: the graph's snapshot release.

from_database.title: From Database
from_database.description: The database the identifiers are meant in; `null`: any.

explain.title: Explain
explain.description: Add the path of every candidate.

allow_bridges.title: Allow Bridges
allow_bridges.description: Allow bridges through ids two genes share when history ends.

BatchRequest.title: BatchRequest
BatchRequest.description: A batch of identifiers converted with the same arguments.

count.title: Count
count.description: The number of results (the number of identifiers given).

results.title: Results
results.description: One result per identifier, in input order.

BatchResponse.title: BatchResponse
BatchResponse.description: The results of a batch, one per identifier, in the order given.

source.title: Source
source.description: The gene the walk would leave.

target.title: Target
target.description: The gene the walk would enter.

places.title: Places
places.description: Where the two genes lie relative to each other: a key of `PLACE_RELATIONS` (the nodes of the path hold both places).

taken.title: Taken
taken.description: The rules allow at least one of the ids in `through` as a bridge (whether a path then uses it depends on the releases and on the other candidates).

through.title: Through
through.description: Every id the two genes carried in common, as `(node, rule)` with a key of `BRIDGE_RULES`; the node is an external id or a transcript.

BridgeCheck.title: BridgeCheck
BridgeCheck.description:
A bridge the search considered from one gene to another, and the rule that took or refused it.

The search considers bridges only where Ensembl's history leads to no gene at the target release, from every gene
the history reached, and only those it can place in time (the far side holds at a release between the near side's
and the target release); every such pair of genes is listed once.

taken.title: Taken
taken.description: A bridge is taken under this rule (`idtrack.results.BRIDGE_RULES_TAKEN`).

BridgeRuleTerm.title: BridgeRuleTerm
BridgeRuleTerm.description: A rule that takes or refuses a bridge (`BridgeCheck.through`), with idtrack's text.

gene.title: Gene
gene.description: The Ensembl gene (`<id>.<version>`) at the target release through which the target was reached.

target.title: Target
target.description: The id in the final database, as that database wrote it at the target release (the gene itself for `ensembl_gene`).

best.title: Best
best.description: Part of the best answer (several candidates are best in a tie).

entry_gene.title: Entry Gene
entry_gene.description: The gene the identifier was read as at the starting release, from which this gene was reached.

entry_databases.title: Entry Databases
entry_databases.description: The databases that attach the identifier to the entry gene at the starting release (for an Ensembl id, the Ensembl relation that reads it: `base_ensembl_gene`, ...); a synonym's database by its own name.

authority.title: Authority
authority.description: A name authority gives the identifier to the entry gene as its symbol at the starting release: HGNC, MGI or VGNC (the symbol databases of the organism) or NCBI's official symbol (`NCBI gene (formerly Entrezgene)`), not as a synonym (decision 94: such a symbol is read before any synonym of another gene, `idtrack.graph.TheGraph.resolve_name`).

display_name.title: Display Name
display_name.description: The identifier is the display name of an entry gene at the starting release (`gene.display_xref_id`: Ensembl's own name of the gene there, whatever database it came from). Among the genes that carry a name at one release such a gene ranks first, before `entry_support` (`idtrack.engine.ranking`; `decided_by` is `"display_name"` where it decided). It holds for the string as typed (decision 102): where the string has letters of both cases, only a display name that its database spelt so; a string in one letter case carries no evidence of case and is read without it. Where the history merges several entry genes into `gene`, this and `display_rank` and `entry_support` are the best over all of them, whichever one `entry_gene` names (the path shown starts from one; decision 106).

display_rank.title: Display Rank
display_rank.description: How the identifier is the display name of an entry gene, as the ranking compares it: 0 the display name (for a string in one letter case in an organism whose symbols are written in mixed case, the display name of a name authority, read without letter case); 1 for such a string, the display name of another source; 2 not its display name (`display_name` is `False` only then).

entry_support.title: Entry Support
entry_support.description: The number of databases that attach the identifier to an entry gene at the starting release (1 for an Ensembl id). For an identifier of digits only, databases of other numbers (an NCBI gene id and a Havana number spelt alike) are not counted against each other: their genes tie (decision 86).

own_version.title: Own Version
own_version.description: The gene is the queried gene id's own version at the target release (an id that exists at the target release is its own answer).

final_confidence.title: Final Confidence
final_confidence.description: 0: the target is attached to the gene at the target release; 1: attached to a transcript or translation that belonged to the gene at another release; `None`: no gene has an id in the requested database and the gene itself is the target.

bridges.title: Bridges
bridges.description: The bridges through external ids (or shared transcripts) on the path; 0 is Ensembl's history alone.

bridge_gap.title: Bridge Gap
bridge_gap.description: The releases between leaving a gene and entering the next, summed over the bridges.

score.title: Score
score.description: The product of Ensembl's mapping scores along the history of the path (1.0 without a scored event).

unscored_steps.title: Unscored Steps
unscored_steps.description: The history steps of the path between two different ids that Ensembl gave no score (it writes 0 where it measured nothing); a path with such a step ranks below every path whose scores are measured, before `score` compares them (decision 57).

same_as_query.title: Same As Query
same_as_query.description: The target is the identifier itself (or the gene id it was read as).

annotation.title: Annotation
annotation.description: `(-external ids, -transcripts, -translations)` of the gene at the target release, where the engine compared it (between successors of one entry gene that are equal in everything else); `None` where it did not.

path.title: Path
path.description: With `explain`: the indices of `ExplainedPath.steps` from the identifier to `gene`, in order; empty otherwise.

final_path.title: Final Path
final_path.description: With `explain`: the indices of the steps from `gene` to `target` (empty when the gene is the target).

Candidate.title: Candidate
Candidate.description:
One target of a conversion: a gene at the target release and its id in the requested database.

The fields after `best` are the ranking record of the candidate: what the engine compared.

graph_id.title: Graph Id
graph_id.description: The identifier of the graph the identifier was read as (`None`: not found). For an Ensembl transcript or translation id without version this is its version of the starting release. A synonym is written as it is (`match` says it is a synonym).

match.title: Match
match.description: How the identifier matched `graph_id`: a step of `MATCH_STEPS` after the prefixes of `MATCH_PREFIXES` that apply (`"synonym:exact"`, `"unicode:case"`); `None` when it is not in the graph.

known_versions.title: Known Versions
known_versions.description: For an Ensembl id, or a sequence accession, written with a version the graph does not hold: the versions that exist (the identifier is not answered with another version's gene).

from_release.title: From Release
from_release.description: The release at which the identifier was read.

from_release_inferred.title: From Release Inferred
from_release_inferred.description: The release was chosen by the engine, not given.

from_release_fallback.title: From Release Fallback
from_release_fallback.description: The release given was set aside because the graph does not hold the identifier there; it was read where the graph holds it.

from_databases.title: From Databases
from_databases.description: For an external id, the databases through which it was read at that release (for a synonym: the databases that record it).

final_database.title: Final Database
final_database.description: The database of the targets: the requested one, `ensembl_gene` when the genes reached have no id in it (`no_target`), `None` when nothing was found.

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.description: Every target reached, ranked, the best first and marked.

tie.title: Tie
tie.description: The best answer is shared by several genes or targets equal in all evidence.

decided_by.title: Decided By
decided_by.description: The criterion (`CRITERIA`) that put the best answer before the runner-up; `None` without a runner-up.

alternative_locus_genes.title: Alternative Locus Genes
alternative_locus_genes.description: Copies on alternative loci and patches, LRG records, and the Y copies of pseudoautosomal genes (beside their gene on X), that the identifier also leads to beside genes of the reference sequence; not candidates.

no_target.title: No Target
no_target.description: Genes were reached, but none has an id in the requested database; the candidates are the genes.

no_target_genes.title: No Target Genes
no_target_genes.description: Genes reached without an id in the requested database while others have one; not candidates.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: The first of `reasons`; `None` when none applies.

reasons.title: Reasons
reasons.description: Every reason that applies, keys of `REASONS`, in this order: why the result has no target in the requested database (no candidates, or `no_target`: genes stand in for the missing id); `"read_at_another_release"` where the identifier was read at another release than the one given (`from_release_fallback`); `"version_not_judged"` where a version written after an accession was not judged (decision 101). Empty for a result with targets read as asked.

other_readings.title: Other Readings
other_readings.description: The other nodes the identifier was read as: those a rule of name resolution put after `graph_id`, with what they would answer, those read by the same step, whose candidates are part of a tie, and those the string has at other releases only, with those releases (`idtrack.graph.TheGraph.readings`).

error.description: In a batch, the error that stopped this identifier's conversion.

path.description: With `explain`: the paths of the candidates (no step when there is no candidate) and the bridges the search considered; `None` without `explain`.

ConversionResult.title: ConversionResult
ConversionResult.description: One identifier converted to a target release and database (`idtrack.API.convert`).

first.title: First
first.description: Which value ranks first: `yes` (true before false), `lower` or `higher` (a tuple compared part by part, from its first part).

parts.title: Parts
parts.description: For a field that is a tuple, the names of its parts, each the negated count (as idtrack's text of the field states); `null` otherwise.

CriterionField.title: CriterionField
CriterionField.description: A `Candidate` field a criterion compares, and which of its values ranks first.

meaning.title: Meaning
meaning.description: idtrack's text of the `Candidate` field of the same name.

fields.title: Fields
fields.description: The fields idtrack's ranking compares for this criterion, in order, the first that differs deciding (the api's reading of `idtrack.engine.ranking`, which gives no such table; tested against idtrack's criteria).

CriterionTerm.title: CriterionTerm
CriterionTerm.description: A criterion that ranks candidates: idtrack's text of its field, and the fields its ranking compares.

code.title: Code
code.description: A stable code of the kind of error (SETUP.md and README.md list them).

message.title: Message
message.description: What went wrong and what to change, in words.

argument.title: Argument
argument.description: The argument the error is about, where one is.

allowed.title: Allowed
allowed.description: The values the argument accepts, where they can be listed.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description: The id of the request; quote it when reporting an internal error.

ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody
ErrorBody.description: An error: a stable code, a message that says what to change, and the request's id.

input_error.title: Input Error
input_error.description: `True` when the error is the caller's (`idtrack.errors.InputError`), `False` for any other (an exceeded budget, an internal error).

ErrorInfo.title: ErrorInfo
ErrorInfo.description: An error that stopped the conversion of one identifier in a batch.

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description: The body of every response that is not a success.

status.title: Status
status.description: The HTTP status it is answered with.

meaning.title: Meaning
meaning.description: When it is answered, and what to change.

ErrorTerm.title: ErrorTerm
ErrorTerm.description: An error code of the api, its status and when it is answered.

nodes.title: Nodes
nodes.description: The nodes of every step and of every bridge considered, ordered by first use.

steps.title: Steps
steps.description: The steps of every candidate's path, each once, ordered by first use.

bridges.title: Bridges
bridges.description: Every bridge the search considered, taken or refused, with its rule (empty when Ensembl's history alone reached the target release); ordered by source and target.

refused.title: Refused
refused.description: The history steps of Ensembl the search did not follow, in the direction of the walk, each with the rule that refused it as its `PathStep.reason` (a step between the mitochondrial genome and a nuclear sequence); ordered by source, target and key.

ExplainedPath.title: ExplainedPath
ExplainedPath.description: The paths of a conversion as one graph: every node and step once; candidates refer to steps by index.

final_databases.title: Final Databases
final_databases.description: The values `final_database` accepts for this release.

FinalDatabasesResponse.title: FinalDatabasesResponse
FinalDatabasesResponse.description: The databases a conversion to a release can end in.

assembly.title: Assembly
assembly.description: The assembly key of idtrack's organism table.

region.title: Region
region.description: The sequence region as Ensembl names it (a chromosome, a scaffold, a patch).

start.title: Start
start.description: The first base of the gene (1-based).

end.title: End
end.description: The last base of the gene (inclusive).

releases.title: Releases
releases.description: The inclusive release ranges at which the gene lies there.

reference.title: Reference
reference.description: The region is part of the reference sequence (not a patch, a haplotype, an alternative locus or an LRG record).

GenePlace.title: GenePlace
GenePlace.description: Where a gene lies at some releases: an assembly, a sequence region, its first and last base, a strand.

primary_assembly.title: Primary Assembly
primary_assembly.description: The assembly of the graph's snapshot release.

snapshot_release.title: Snapshot Release
snapshot_release.description: The last release of the graph.

assemblies.title: Assemblies
assemblies.description: The assemblies, by the organism table's priority.

serving_assembly.title: Serving Assembly
serving_assembly.description: Release (as a string, a JSON key) to the assembly that serves it.

external_databases.title: External Databases
external_databases.description: The external databases of the graph (any assembly), as `idtrack.API.external_databases` names them.

final_databases.title: Final Databases
final_databases.description: The databases a conversion to the snapshot release can end in.

forms.title: Forms
forms.description: The Ensembl forms of the graph (`gene`, `transcript`, `translation`).

format_version.title: Format Version
format_version.description: The graph file's format version (`None` for a graph made in memory).

package_version.title: Package Version
package_version.description: The idtrack version that built the graph.

package_commit.title: Package Commit
package_commit.description: The git commit of idtrack that built the graph, where it was known.

content_digest.title: Content Digest
content_digest.description: The digest of the graph's content.

counts.title: Counts
counts.description: Counts of the build (nodes, edges, ...), as the graph file records them.

GraphDescription.title: GraphDescription
GraphDescription.description: What a loaded graph holds (`idtrack.API.describe`), read from the graph without the network.

key.title: Key
key.description: The key of the file in the store: `idtrack/<format>/<organism>/<sha256>.npz`.

sha256.title: Sha256
sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the file's bytes, verified before loading.

size.title: Size
size.description: The size of the file in bytes.

GraphFile.title: GraphFile
GraphFile.description: A published file as the server verified it.

snapshot_release.title: Snapshot Release
snapshot_release.description: The last Ensembl release of the graph.

content_digest.title: Content Digest
content_digest.description: The digest of the graph's content, as its build recorded it.

package_version.title: Package Version
package_version.description: The idtrack version that built the graph.

package_commit.title: Package Commit
package_commit.description: The idtrack commit that built the graph, where known.

GraphVersion.title: GraphVersion
GraphVersion.description: What a loaded graph is and what built it.

status.title: Status
status.description: Always `ok` (a server that is not ready does not answer).

organisms.title: Organisms
organisms.description: The organisms whose graphs this server holds.

HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse
HealthResponse.description: The server is up and its graphs are loaded.

batch_max.title: Batch Max
batch_max.description: The most identifiers of one batch.

identifier_max_length.title: Identifier Max Length
identifier_max_length.description: The longest identifier or name, in characters.

body_max_bytes.title: Body Max Bytes
body_max_bytes.description: The largest request body, in bytes.

response_max_bytes.title: Response Max Bytes
response_max_bytes.description: The largest answer, in bytes; a larger one is refused, never cut.

request_seconds.title: Request Seconds
request_seconds.description: The time budget of one request, in seconds.

search_seconds.title: Search Seconds
search_seconds.description: The time budget of one identifier's search, in seconds.

search_states.title: Search States
search_states.description: The most search states one identifier's search may expand.

rate_per_minute.title: Rate Per Minute
rate_per_minute.description: Requests per minute per client (0: no limit).

rate_burst.title: Rate Burst
rate_burst.description: Requests a client may make at once before the rate applies.

queue_max.title: Queue Max
queue_max.description: Requests one worker holds, running or waiting, before answering `503`.

LimitsResponse.title: LimitsResponse
LimitsResponse.description: The bounds this server enforces, as configured (SETUP.md, "Configuration").

name.title: Name
name.description: The name as the link of the gene writes it at these releases.

database.title: Database
database.description: The database (for a synonym: the database that records it).

synonym.title: Synonym
synonym.description: The name is one of the database's synonyms of the gene, not its name.

releases.title: Releases
releases.description: The releases at which the database attaches the name to the gene on the assembly that serves each, and the gene lies on the reference sequence, ascending.

NameMatch.title: NameMatch
NameMatch.description: A name of an external database attached to an Ensembl gene, and the releases at which it is.

matches.title: Matches
matches.description: The matches, as idtrack orders them.

NamesResponse.title: NamesResponse
NamesResponse.description: Names and the genes they name, per database and release.

OrganismsResponse.title: OrganismsResponse
OrganismsResponse.description: Every loaded organism and what its graph holds.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why it is reported: a key of `READING_REASONS`.

genes.title: Genes
genes.description: The genes of the best answer that a conversion of this reading gives (the same target release and arguments), ascending; empty when it gives none.

releases.title: Releases
releases.description: For a reading of reason `other_release`, the releases at which the string has this meaning, ascending; empty otherwise.

OtherReading.title: OtherReading
OtherReading.description: Another graph node an identifier was read as, beside `ConversionResult.graph_id`.

id.title: Id
id.description: The node's id within the explanation: the identifier (a synonym written as it is, without the graph's bookkeeping; `synonym:<text>` only should the same text name another node of the explanation).

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: `ensembl_gene`, `base_ensembl_gene`, `ensembl_transcript`, `ensembl_translation`, `external` or `synonym` (an external id recorded as a synonym).

label.title: Label
label.description: The name to show for the node: the identifier.

databases.title: Databases
databases.description: For an external id, the databases that attach it to an Ensembl id at some release (for a synonym, the databases that record it); empty otherwise.

active.title: Active
active.description: For an Ensembl gene with version, the inclusive release ranges in which it exists (`None`: still active at the last release of the graph); empty otherwise.

assemblies.title: Assemblies
assemblies.description: For an Ensembl gene with version, the assemblies that serve its active releases.

non_reference.title: Non Reference
non_reference.description: For an Ensembl gene, the release ranges in which it lies outside the reference sequence (an alternative locus, a patch, an LRG record).

places.title: Places
places.description: For an Ensembl gene with version, where it lies at its releases (on the assembly that serves each release); empty otherwise.

PathNode.title: PathNode
PathNode.description: A node of an explained path.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: `identity` (the gene is its own answer), `entry` (from the identifier to the gene it stands for), `history` (an event of Ensembl's id history), `self_loop` (a scored re-mapping of a gene to itself), `bridge_near` and `bridge_far` (the two sides of a bridge through an id two genes carry), `final` (from the gene to its id in the final database).

source.title: Source
source.description: The node the step leaves (`None` for `identity`).

key.title: Key
key.description: The key of a history edge (Ensembl events between the same two ids); `None` otherwise.

release.title: Release
release.description: The release at which a cross-reference step holds (`None` for a final step of confidence 1, which holds at another release).

old_release.title: Old Release
old_release.description: For a history step: the old side of Ensembl's event, the last release of the event's earlier id. Ensembl's events run forward in time, the walk may not: walking forward the earlier id is `source`, walking backward (to an earlier target release) it is `target`.

new_release.title: New Release
new_release.description: For a history step: the new side of the event, the first release of the event's later id (`target` walking forward, `source` walking backward).

weight.title: Weight
weight.description: For a history step: Ensembl's mapping score (`None`: none given).

splits.title: Splits
splits.description: For a history step: the other ids that the event's earlier id passed to at `old_release` (a split), whatever the direction of the walk.

merges.title: Merges
merges.description: For a history step: the other ids that passed to the event's later id at `new_release` (a merge), whatever the direction of the walk.

databases.title: Databases
databases.description: For a cross-reference step: the databases that link the two nodes at the release on the assembly that serves it (for a synonym: the databases that record it).

assembly.title: Assembly
assembly.description: The assembly that serves `release` (or, for a history step, `new_release`, the event's new side).

old_assembly.title: Old Assembly
old_assembly.description: For a history step: the assembly that serves `old_release`, the event's old side (it differs from `assembly` where the event crosses from one assembly to the next); `None` otherwise.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the step was taken (or, for a step of `ExplainedPath.refused`, why it was not): a key of `STEP_REASONS`.

places.title: Places
places.description: For a history step between two genes: where the event's later gene lies relative to the earlier one (a key of `PLACE_RELATIONS`; `places_apart`: Ensembl's history moves the gene to another place, which the walk follows); `None` for other steps.

PathStep.title: PathStep
PathStep.description: A step of an explained path.

code.title: Code
code.description: The code, as answers carry it.

meaning.title: Meaning
meaning.description: What it means, in the defining table's words; `null` where that table gives no text.

source.title: Source
source.description: Whose words `meaning` is: `idtrack` (its own table, `idtrack.results`), or `idtrack-web` (the api's own table, kept where idtrack gives no text, and tested against idtrack's set of codes).

Term.title: Term
Term.description: A code of the api's answers and what it means, from the one place that defines it.

location.title: Location
location.description: Where the problem is: `query`, `path` or `body`, then the field.

ValidationDetail.title: ValidationDetail
ValidationDetail.description: One problem of a request that does not have the shape the endpoint takes.

idtrack_version.title: Idtrack Version
idtrack_version.description: The version of idtrack that answers.

idtrack_commit.title: Idtrack Commit
idtrack_commit.description: The idtrack commit that answers, where known.

graph_format_version.title: Graph Format Version
graph_format_version.description: The graph file format this idtrack reads.

manifest.description: The manifest the graphs were read from.

VersionResponse.title: VersionResponse
VersionResponse.description: The versions of the server, of idtrack and of each loaded graph.

statuses.title: Statuses
statuses.description: The values of `ConversionResult.status`, in idtrack's order.

criteria.title: Criteria
criteria.description: The values of `ConversionResult.decided_by`, in the order in which they decide (idtrack's `CRITERIA`); each criterion is the `Candidate` field of the same name, and its meaning is that field's text.

candidate_fields.title: Candidate Fields
candidate_fields.description: Every field of `Candidate`, in order, with idtrack's text of it (its ranking record).

match_prefixes.title: Match Prefixes
match_prefixes.description: The parts of a match before its step, each followed by `:`, in this order (idtrack's `MATCH_PREFIXES`).

VocabularyResponse.title: VocabularyResponse
VocabularyResponse.description:
What the codes of the answers mean: idtrack's own tables, and the api's tables where idtrack gives no text.

Every code is idtrack's (``idtrack.results``: ``STATUSES``, ``REASONS``, ``STEP_REASONS``, ``CRITERIA``,
``MATCH_STEPS``, ``MATCH_PREFIXES``, ``READING_REASONS``, ``PLACE_RELATIONS``, ``BRIDGE_RULES``), with idtrack's
text wherever it gives one; a criterion's meaning is idtrack's text of the ``Candidate`` field it compares. Where
idtrack gives codes without texts (``STATUSES``) the meaning is the api's (``source`` says so), and the fields a
criterion compares are the api's reading of idtrack's ranking; both are tested against idtrack's codes.
